Three quick framing rules — they fix almost every "weird diagnosis".
Too close: only a tiny patch is in frame. Too far: the leaf is a thumbnail. Aim so one leaf fills most of the frame.
Tap the leaf to lock autofocus. Avoid back-lit shots — the leaf should not be a dark silhouette against a bright window.
Mixing two plants in one photo confuses both the classifier and the species detector. Crop or step back to isolate a single plant.

Colorful or mottled patterns on ornamental foliage (Calathea, Caladium, Coleus, Croton, Aglaonema…) can closely resemble viral mosaic. If this is a variegated cultivar, the pattern may be perfectly normal — compare with a healthy leaf of the same plant and consider a second opinion before treating.

How to take a good scan photo

Fill the frame with a single leaf, use daylight, and hold the phone steady — the scanner auto-fires when the frame is sharp. Avoid backlight and wet, glossy reflections; photograph the most affected leaf, including some healthy tissue for contrast.

The confidence score is calibrated: when the app isn\'t sure it shows several candidate conditions instead of guessing. Treat the result as guidance, check the alternatives card, and use a second photo or the symptom checker when the model says it\'s uncertain.

Overwatering kills more houseplants than drought. Check the top 2–3 cm of soil with a finger — water only when it\'s dry, then water thoroughly until it drains. Use the Watering helper for a per-plant starting point and adjust by season.
